name: Deploy (GitHub)
description: Run deployment pipelines under signed human authority

resolve_ref.readGovernanceReason: Returns a commit pointer only — SHA, subject line, author, date. Repository metadata, not user content, and scoped to permitted repos. An age window over 'what commit is main' would govern nothing.

list_deployments.readGovernanceReason: Returns run metadata only — id, status, commit, timestamp. No build output and no user content. Scoped to permitted repos. Build logs, which CAN carry secrets and content, are a separate tool and will be age-bounded when added.

get_deployment.readGovernanceReason: Returns run metadata only — id, status, commit, timestamp. No build output. Scoped to permitted repos.

list_environments.readGovernanceReason: Returns environment names only. Repository configuration, not content, and needed so the owner can choose a target that actually exists.

templates.name: Watch deploys
templates.description: Read deployment status and history. Cannot deploy anything.
templates.intent: Let the agent see what has been deployed and whether a release succeeded. It may not deploy: a daily maximum of zero is a real limit, not an unset one. Fill in allowed_repos with the repositories it may look at.

templates.name: Deploy production, review
templates.description: Deploy a specific commit after approval. Three per day, no rollback.
templates.intent: The agent may propose deploying a specific commit to production; nothing runs until I approve it. Always resolve the branch to a commit first — I approve a commit, not a branch, so that what I reviewed is what ships. Fill in allowed_repos, and check that allowed_environments matches what the host actually calls it (GitHub uses the names you defined, Vercel uses production and preview).

setupHint: Create a fine-grained token scoped to ONE repository. The agent deploys commits that already exist — it never needs permission to write code.

setupGuide.title: Create a fine-grained token
setupGuide.description: On GitHub go to Settings, Developer settings, Personal access tokens, Fine-grained tokens. Do not use a classic token: those grant access to everything you own, which is the standing-authority problem this integration exists to remove.

setupGuide.title: Scope it to one repository
setupGuide.description: Under Repository access choose Only select repositories, and pick the single repository you want the agent to deploy.

setupGuide.title: Grant three permissions
setupGuide.description: Actions: Read and write (to start the pipeline). Environments: Read (to see which environments exist). Contents: Read (to turn a branch into a commit). Do NOT grant Contents: Write — the agent ships commits that exist, it never writes them.

setupGuide.title: Paste the token below
setupGuide.description: It is encrypted in your local vault. The agent never sees it: the gateway uses it on the agent's behalf, and only after checking the deploy against your signed limits.
